title: spec: WebhookSchema marks secret and headers as credential fields; the redactor registry derives meta read-door redaction from the schema (ruling B+ on #24966)
body:
Closes #24994
Refs #24966
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What the ruling binds (B+ on #24966, record 6304303975)

Quoted from the ruling record, items as recorded:

> 1. **The marker, in spec.** `WebhookSchema.secret` and `WebhookSchema.headers` are declared credential fields with a schema-level marker (zod `.meta({ credential: … })`, the repo's existing `.meta` convention), `headers` as a whole map. The fact "this field is a credential" lives on the declaration, once.
> 2. **The derivation, once, in the kernel registry.** `getMetadataTypeRedactor(type)` resolves, after the explicit registrations and built-ins, a redactor DERIVED from the type's registered schema: every marked field is dropped (not masked) and served as its cleared form, and `redactedKeys` names them. Any metadata type that marks a field is redacted on every meta read door with nothing else to write. `webhook` is the first type served this way.
> 3. **The guard.** A spec ratchet test reads every registered metadata-type schema and fails when a field whose name or description reads as a credential (secret, password, token, signing, api key, credential) carries no marker and sits on no explicit allow-list — the fail-closed half the datasource module asked for.
> 4. **Unchanged from B:** the redaction form (`secret` and the whole `headers` map dropped, cleared forms served), the write-path carry-forward accepted, delivery signing and door reach untouched. `datasource` and `flow` keep their explicit redactors (they take precedence over the derivation) and are not migrated.
> 5. **Standing word, recorded here:** 「类似的问题都可以这样处理」 — where a per-type behaviour is a function of the declared shape, declare the fact on the schema and derive the behaviour once in the kernel, rather than writing a per-type function. Seats cite this ruling when the same choice recurs.

Disclosure: the maintainer's ruling on #9387 (`5323310017`) applies. This PR carries location, rule and abstract reach only.

## What changed

- **The marker** (`packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts`): `secret` carries `.meta({ credential: 'value' })` and `headers` carries `.meta({ credential: 'map' })`. Nothing else about the schema changes: no key is added, removed or re-typed. The marker key is `credential` and its vocabulary is closed: `value` (one credential, cleared form the empty string) and `map` (a map whose entries cannot be told apart, so the whole map is the credential, cleared form the empty map).
- **The derivation** (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.ts`, new, not re-exported from the `kernel` barrel): walks the type's declared object shape and each nested object shape below it (through optional, nullable, default, pipe and lazy wrappers), collects the marked fields, and builds a pure redactor. It is memoised per schema identity, so the walk runs once per schema, not per read.
- **The third resolution** (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts`): `getMetadataTypeRedactor(type)` resolves explicit registration, then built-in, then the redactor derived from `getMetadataTypeSchema(type)`. `listMetadataTypeRedactorTypes()` now includes the types whose schema derives one. The module note records the ruling and the precedence.
- **The guard** (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.test.ts`): the ratchet, described below.
- **Door pins** (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/webhook-meta-door-credential-redaction.dogfood.test.ts`), in both compositions.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/24994-webhook-credential-marker.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, with a **BREAKING** banner and a `spec!:` headline. The declaration is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and the ADR-0087 disposition is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. During the launch window a narrowing ships as `minor`, not `patch`. That rule comes from `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (maintainer ruling 2026-09-04, batch #35, on #15294) and outranks the card's `patch` workload line. Every `no (narrowing)` changeset on main is graded `minor`, and this one now is too.

### The served form, read precisely

A marked field that holds credential material is **removed** from the served item and named in `redactedKeys`. A stored cleared form (an empty-string `secret`, an empty `headers` map) holds nothing, so it is served as written and not reported. This is how the governing precedents put it: the `flow` projection's "Dropped, not masked", and the dev report's option A ("keys removed, not masked; serve the two cleared forms as written … so a reader tells 'cleared' from 'withheld'"). It is also what ruling item 5 of the card needs: the carry-forward keeps the stored values for a save that **omits** the two fields. If the cleared form were put in place of the withheld value, a save of the served body would be indistinguishable from a deliberate clear. A reviewer who reads card item 2 ("serves its cleared form") as "substitute the cleared form" should note that this reading was weighed and not taken, for that reason.

### The ratchet, and what "reads as a credential" means

- The schema set is `listMetadataTypeSchemaTypes()` **plus** `listUnregisteredKindSchemaTypes()`. `webhook` is a stack-collection kind bound in `UNREGISTERED_KIND_SCHEMAS`, not in the registered-kind list, so the first list alone would not read the one type this card is about. `getMetadataTypeSchema('webhook')` resolves through that map, and the derivation reads it from there.
- A field the walk reaches reads as a credential when its name, split into words, contains secret / password / passwd / token / signing / credential (or a plural), or `api` then `key`; or when the first sentence of its description contains one of those words. Only fields that can hold a credential count: a string, a record, a union, an unknown. A number, boolean, enum or array cannot hold a secret, and without this limit token budgets would be flagged.
- Allow-list: one entry, `datasource:external.credentialsRef`. It is a reference into the secrets store, never the credential itself. A pin fails if an entry stops matching a field the rule flags, so the list cannot rot.
- Two more pins keep the marker honest: every marker uses the closed vocabulary and a `map` marker sits on a record; and no marker sits where the derivation cannot reach it (inside an array, a union or a record value). A probe test checks that the second pin can see such a marker.
- A synthetic case shows the ratchet fails on an unmarked credential-named field (top-level and nested) and passes once that field is marked.

### Unchanged (ruling item 5 of the card)

- **The write-path carry-forward** still keys on "a redactor resolves for the type". A save of the served form keeps the stored values; the dogfood file pins it in both compositions.
- **The dispatcher's declared-webhook source** reads the registry's raw declaration and re-parses it, never a served copy. Pinned with plugin-webhooks mounted: both credentials are still present there, so delivery signing is unaffected.
- **Who may reach a meta read door** does not change.
- **plugin-webhooks** registers nothing.
- **`datasource` and `flow`** keep their explicit redactors, which take precedence. A unit test pins that an explicit registration wins over the derivation and that the datasource built-in still resolves.

## Door pins (both compositions: without plugin-webhooks, and with it mounted)

Each pin reads one door and asserts three things by rule: the read answers 200, it names the webhook (a positive control, so a refusal or an empty answer cannot pass), and it holds neither declared credential field. The doors:

- the meta list, both spellings
- the item read
- the layered view
- the published read
- the metadata protocol's list and item reads
- the stored-row data door and its history twin

Meta doors are read as an administrator and as a signed-in member. The data door is read as an administrator, the only caller who can reach it. The fixture's credentials are obviously-fake placeholders.

## Verification (head `0cf6eed565`)

- `@objectstack/spec`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` green (run at `441ce0128d`; the later commit touches only the walker's definition read and adds one test). At `0cf6eed565`: the two touched files `src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.test.ts` and `src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.test.ts` give 2 files and 39 tests passed, and `typecheck` passed. After `spec build`, `check:generated` reports all 14 generated artifacts up to date, so no artifact regenerated. No public export was added: the new module is not re-exported from the `kernel` barrel, and `check:api-surface` is green.
- `@objectstack/rest`: `test` green at `0cf6eed565` (307 files; 6157 passed, 326 skipped), and `typecheck` passed. An earlier head failed `rest-exposure-gate-execution-read.test.ts`, and the cause was in this PR. That test wraps the registered `object` schema in a second Proxy. A `_zod` read through a Proxy over a `lazySchema` Proxy throws a Proxy invariant error, so the walk read that way turned the instrumented type's meta reads into 500s. The walker now reads the public `.def`, and a unit test pins derivation through a doubly proxied schema.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`: `test` and `typecheck` green (run at `441ce0128d`). `@objectstack/dogfood` `typecheck` is green.
- Dogfood at `0cf6eed565`: the new pin file plus `webhook-materialization` and `wall-declared-webhook-deployment-wide` give 3 files and 24 tests passed.
- **Ablation** (marker removed, the pin reads red). Both `credential` markers on `WebhookSchema` were rewritten to a non-marker key through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 to 0 for each, on-disk counts 0 and 0. `@objectstack/spec` was rebuilt, and `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs --absent` confirmed both markers absent from all 232 built files. The pin file then read 12 failed and 3 passed. The 3 that stayed green are the two composition guards and the dispatcher-source pin, which do not depend on redaction. Restore: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty, spec rebuilt, the preflight confirmed both markers present in 18 built files, and the pin file read 15 of 15 passed. A first attempt was refused by the replace tool before anything ran, because its replacement-count check rejected the anchor shape; nothing was mutated, and that attempt counts for nothing.
- Derived gate families (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 87 families): all 87 run, with the spec and changeset subset run again at `0cf6eed565`, and all exit 0 except one. `check:type-check-debt` was run under the lock at `0cf6eed565`: the re-measure is OK, and no ledger entry is above its recorded number. The exception: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is NOT MEASURED, because it needs every workspace package built and only the dogfood closure was built. That one is declared to CI.


### Fix round (head `e86f32235f`)

This round merged `origin/main` and re-graded the changeset to `minor`, adding the BREAKING banner. The changeset gates all exit 0: `check-changeset-no-major` (`--base origin/main` and `--self-test`), `check-adr-0087-registration` (both), `check-empty-changeset` (both), and `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`. After them, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` passed 703 files and 21388 tests (1 skipped, 1 todo), and `typecheck` passed. Both ran under the lock, with VERDICT command-exit 0. The `dispatch-gates --commands` derivation is unchanged from the previous head (same 87 families). The gates this round's delta touches also exit 0: `check:nul-bytes`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:pm-changeset-deadline-census`, closing-keyword parity, `check:objectui-changeset` and `check:closed-ceremony-text`.

## Acceptance notes

- `.meta({ credential })` is carried into the generated JSON Schema of a webhook (zod copies metadata into the JSON Schema node), so `/meta/types` and the IDE schema now show `credential: 'value' | 'map'` on the two properties. This is an annotation only: no gate artifact changed (`check:generated` reports all 14 up to date).
- The derivation reads a type's schema the first time that type's redactor is resolved, which means a lazily built schema is built on its first meta read. This is memoised per schema identity.
- MCP: the card's door list does not name an MCP door. The dev report on #24966 measured that the MCP HTTP tools refuse the stored metadata objects, and that the stdio data bridge applies the same stored-row projection this registry drives. No MCP pin is added here.
